title: The open-closed short exact sequence of an etale sheaf
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of the complementary open subscheme $U=X\setminus i(Z)$. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on the small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], let $j^{-1}F$ and $i^{-1}F$ be the inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], $j_!$ the extension by zero along $j$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and $i_*$ the direct image along $i$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Let $\varepsilon:j_!j^{-1}F\to F$ be the counit of the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ and $\eta:F\to i_*i^{-1}F$ the unit of the adjunction $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$. Then the sequence
$$
0\longrightarrow j_!j^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon\ }F\xrightarrow{\ \eta\ }i_*i^{-1}F\longrightarrow0
$$
is exact in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$. The same holds for sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules for any commutative ring $\Lambda$ (sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules as in [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]) (in particular $\Lambda=\mathbf F_r$), with the same maps.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 095L (label lemma-ses-associated-to-open); its proof compares geometric stalks using Lemma 04FX (lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion) and Proposition 03S5 (proposition-describe-jshriek)

proof.text: Notation and the two kinds of geometric points. Write $G=j^{-1}F$, $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_F:j_!G\to F$ (counit of $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]) and $\eta=\eta_{i,F}:F\to i_*i^{-1}F$ (unit of $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$, [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]); stalks at geometric points are those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Since $i(Z)=X\setminus j(U)$, every geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ [def-weil-geometric-point] is of exactly one of two kinds [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-open-or-closed]: (U) its image lies in $j(U)$ and $\bar x=j\circ\bar u$ for a unique geometric point $\bar u$ of $U$; (Z) its image lies in $i(Z)$ and $\bar x=i\circ\bar z$ for a unique geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$. (Stacks: 'For a geometric point $\bar x$ in $X$ we have either $\bar x\in U$ ... or $\bar x\in Z$'.)

Stalks at $\bar x=j\bar u$ of kind (U): $\varepsilon_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism. The triangle identity of $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ gives $j^{-1}(\varepsilon_F)\circ\eta^!_{j,G}=\mathrm{id}_{G}$, where $\eta^!_{j,G}:G\to j^{-1}j_!G$ is the unit [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]; $\eta^!_{j,G}$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso], so $j^{-1}(\varepsilon_F)=(\eta^!_{j,G})^{-1}$ is an isomorphism, and so is its stalk $(j^{-1}\varepsilon_F)_{\bar u}$. The isomorphisms $c_{j,\bar u,H}:(j^{-1}H)_{\bar u}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{\bar x}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] are natural in $H$, so $c_{j,\bar u,F}\circ(j^{-1}\varepsilon_F)_{\bar u}=\varepsilon_{\bar x}\circ c_{j,\bar u,j_!G}$, and $\varepsilon_{\bar x}=c_{j,\bar u,F}\circ(j^{-1}\varepsilon_F)_{\bar u}\circ c_{j,\bar u,j_!G}^{-1}$ is a composite of isomorphisms. (Stacks: 'the map on the left hand side is an isomorphism on stalks'; Stacks reads this off Proposition 03S5, here it is obtained from the unit isomorphism, which is itself the stalk computation of 03S5 on $U$.)

Stalks at $\bar x$ of kind (U): $(i_*i^{-1}F)_{\bar x}=0$. The closed immersion $i$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction], applied to the abelian sheaf $i^{-1}F$ on $Z_{\Et}$, $(i_*i^{-1}F)_{\bar x}\cong\prod_{\bar z\in P(\bar x)}(i^{-1}F)_{\bar z}$ with $P(\bar x)=\{\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z\mid i\bar z=\bar x\}$. If $i\bar z=\bar x$, the image of $\bar x$ would lie in $i(Z)$, which is disjoint from $j(U)$; so $P(\bar x)=\emptyset$ and the stalk is the empty product $0$. (Stacks Lemma 04FX, first case.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 095L, proof; Lemma 04FX (lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion), case x not in Z

proof.text: Stalks at $\bar x=i\bar z$ of kind (Z): $(j_!G)_{\bar x}=0$ and $\eta_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism. The image of $\bar x$ lies in $i(Z)$, hence not in $j(U)$, so $(j_!G)_{\bar x}=0$ by part 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] (Stacks Proposition 03S5). For $\eta$: the triangle identity of $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] gives $\varepsilon_{i,i^{-1}F}\circ i^{-1}(\eta_{i,F})=\mathrm{id}_{i^{-1}F}$, where the counit $\varepsilon_{i,i^{-1}F}:i^{-1}i_*i^{-1}F\to i^{-1}F$ is an isomorphism because $i$ is a closed immersion [prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful]; hence $i^{-1}(\eta_{i,F})=\varepsilon_{i,i^{-1}F}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism, and so is its stalk at $\bar z$. By naturality of $c_{i,\bar z,H}:(i^{-1}H)_{\bar z}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{\bar x}$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], $c_{i,\bar z,i_*i^{-1}F}\circ(i^{-1}\eta_{i,F})_{\bar z}=\eta_{\bar x}\circ c_{i,\bar z,F}$, so $\eta_{\bar x}$ is a composite of isomorphisms. (Stacks: 'the map on the right hand side is an isomorphism on stalks and the stalk of $j_!j^{-1}F$ is zero', reading off Lemma 04FX, second case; the isomorphism $i^{-1}i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ is that stalk computation in sheaf form.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 095L, proof; Proposition 03S5 (proposition-describe-jshriek); Lemma 04FX (lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion), case x in Z

proof.text: $\eta\circ\varepsilon=0$. For every geometric point $\bar x$, $(\eta\circ\varepsilon)_{\bar x}=\eta_{\bar x}\circ\varepsilon_{\bar x}=0$: for kind (U) its target $(i_*i^{-1}F)_{\bar x}$ is $0$ (step 3), for kind (Z) its source $(j_!G)_{\bar x}$ is $0$ (step 4), and by step 1 there are no other geometric points. $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ is abelian [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]; let $I=\operatorname{im}(\eta\circ\varepsilon)$. The stalk functors are exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], so they preserve images and $I_{\bar x}=\operatorname{im}((\eta\circ\varepsilon)_{\bar x})=0$ for all $\bar x$. Then $I\to0$ is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk, hence an isomorphism [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]; so $I=0$ and $\eta\circ\varepsilon=0$: the sequence is a complex. (Stacks: 'We obtain the maps by the adjointness properties'; that the composite is zero is left implicit there.)

Exactness, from the stalks. Let $K=\ker\varepsilon$, and let $\pi:F\to Q=\operatorname{coker}\varepsilon$; since $\eta\varepsilon=0$ (step 5), $\eta=\bar\eta\circ\pi$ for a unique $\bar\eta:Q\to i_*i^{-1}F$. Stalk functors are exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], so $K_{\bar x}=\ker\varepsilon_{\bar x}$, $Q_{\bar x}=\operatorname{coker}\varepsilon_{\bar x}$ with $\pi_{\bar x}$ the projection, and $\bar\eta_{\bar x}$ is the map induced by $\eta_{\bar x}$. At $\bar x$ of kind (U), $\varepsilon_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism (step 2), so $K_{\bar x}=0$, $Q_{\bar x}=0$, and $\bar\eta_{\bar x}:0\to(i_*i^{-1}F)_{\bar x}=0$ (step 3) is an isomorphism. At $\bar x$ of kind (Z), the source of $\varepsilon_{\bar x}$ is $0$ (step 4), so $K_{\bar x}=0$, $\pi_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism and $\bar\eta_{\bar x}=\eta_{\bar x}\circ\pi_{\bar x}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism (step 4). By step 1 this covers all geometric points. Hence $K\to0$ and $\bar\eta$ are isomorphisms on every geometric stalk, hence isomorphisms [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]: $\varepsilon$ is a monomorphism and $\eta=\bar\eta\pi$ is, up to the isomorphism $\bar\eta$, the cokernel of $\varepsilon$. So $0\to j_!j^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}F\xrightarrow{\eta}i_*i^{-1}F\to0$ is exact in the abelian category $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]: $\varepsilon$ is injective, $\eta$ surjective and $\ker\eta=\ker\pi=\operatorname{im}\varepsilon$. (Stacks: the stalkwise statements of the proof, which suffice because exactness is checked on geometric stalks.)

Sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ and $\operatorname{For}$ the functor to the underlying abelian sheaf. The functors commute with $\operatorname{For}$: $j_!$ because $j_{p!}$ is formed sectionwise on the underlying presheaves [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and sheafification of presheaves of $\Lambda$-modules has the sheafification of the underlying presheaf of abelian groups as underlying sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]; $j^{-1}$, $i^{-1}$ by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] part 2 (with $\Lambda_U=j^{-1}\Lambda_X$, $\Lambda_Z=i^{-1}\Lambda_X$); $i_*$ because it is formed sectionwise [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The maps are the same: the counit $\varepsilon$ of the $\Lambda$-linear $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ is induced by the identity maps $F(V)\to F(V)$ for $V$ factoring through $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], as is the abelian one; the abelian unit $\eta_{i,\operatorname{For}F}$ is $\Lambda$-linear (by naturality in $F$, applied to multiplication by each $\lambda\in\Lambda$), and since the adjunction bijection $\Hom(i^{-1}F,H)\cong\Hom(F,i_*H)$ of abelian sheaves is natural in $F$ and $H$ it restricts to the $\Lambda$-linear maps, so this unit is the unit of the $\Lambda$-linear adjunction. Thus $\operatorname{For}$ maps the $\Lambda$-module sequence to the abelian sequence of $\operatorname{For}F$, which is exact by step 6. $\operatorname{For}$ is faithful and exact [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], so it preserves kernels, cokernels and images and reflects zero objects ($\operatorname{For}A=0$ gives $\operatorname{For}(\mathrm{id}_A)=0=\operatorname{For}(0)$, so $\mathrm{id}_A=0$); hence the $\Lambda$-module sequence has zero kernel of $\varepsilon$, zero cokernel of $\eta$ and zero homology at $F$, i.e. it is exact in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. For $\Lambda=\mathbf F_r$ this is the case used by [lem-weil-pbc-curve-dense-open-localization].

Statement: 'any ring' corrected to 'any commutative ring' (the definition of sheaves of Lambda-modules and of j_! is for commutative Lambda); stmt_deps gained def-weil-open-immersion and lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction (the counit).
